scope: Every reusable element across 17 states: Draft (4), Settings (6), Mock Lab (7).
method: Named by what the element claims, not where it sits. Two elements with the same claim are one component with variants, even if they were built twice.

components.name: ValuePair
components.claim: Two values shown together, where collapsing them into one would hide whether the system is reasoning from current state.

variants.label: baseline → live
variants.treatment: baseline quiet (--dim2, small) · arrow · live loud (600, band-coloured)

variants.label: in force → edited
variants.treatment: in-force struck through (--dim2) · arrow · edited (--down, 600) · row lifted to --panel2

states: second value null (renders the not-yet reason, never the first value again)
components.find: THESE WERE BUILT TWICE UNDER TWO NAMES. Same claim, same rule, different code. Consolidating them is the single highest-value merge in this audit.
components.rule: The second value never replaces the first. Any component-level API must make it impossible to render one alone.

components.name: ValueCell
components.claim: A number and the epistemic status of that number.

variants.treatment: --txt, no marking
--dim2 + --hatch background + † dagger + section tag
— in --dim2, reason on hover, no hatch
<1% — a real value below the display floor
pre-edit value at full contrast, banner carries the pending status

components.rule: Four glyph claims are distinct and must never substitute: —, <1%, 0%, 'not yet'.

components.name: FrequencyDots
components.claim: A probability read as a frequency, so it cannot be misread as a precise scalar.

variants.note: the value is actionable, so colour carries urgency

variants.fill: --txt neutral + ▲ marker beneath at the stated index
variants.note: the value is being audited, so colour must not editorialise

components.find: Five sizes for one idiom, and two different fill rules. The fill rules are DEFENSIBLE and should be documented as variants; the five sizes are drift and are now three.
components.rule: fill = round(p*10). Never print more precision than the model supports.

components.name: Chip
components.claim: A short label. Radius and interactivity encode what kind.

variants.example: ALL / QB / RB · R1–R16 · state switcher
QB ×2 needs chip · CURRENT / STALE status

components.find: FIVE treatments were in use where three were intended. Rule now explicit: rounded = interactive filter, pill = display-only and non-sortable, square = structural label or verdict.
components.rule: A pill must never be sortable or act as a filter — the product's credibility depends on display-only labels never appearing to influence a rank.

components.name: StatusBanner
components.claim: A state that is true across the whole app right now, and survives navigation.
components.find: Mock Lab has no banner and needs one — see AUDIT STALE-01.
components.rule: Persists across route changes; it is the only always-visible carrier of app-wide state.

components.name: Progress
components.claim: How far through something, or how much evidence exists.

variants.treatment: 5px bar + 26px percent + named stage list (✓ ▸ ·)
3px, full width, no label
6px bar + tempo + ETA from real timestamps
30 squares 15px, --r-c 3px
one row per sample size, bar = real Wilson half-width

components.find: FIVE progress treatments across two screens. Four are justified (job vs count vs target vs evidence are different claims); the 3px banner rail and the 5px job bar are the SAME claim at two heights — normalise to 3px in banners, 5px in panels, and say so.
components.rule: No badges, streaks, levels or congratulation anywhere.

components.name: Disclosure
components.claim: More detail, one interaction away, without leaving the row.

variants.treatment: 1px dotted underline + cursor:help → glossary popover
14–15px circle with i → same popover
native title — the fallback for any truncated or dense value
--f-num 9–10px --dim2 naming the backing field
'why' toggle expanding the derivation inside the row container
one line naming everything missing at once

components.find: SIX disclosure patterns, all legitimate, but they were never named as a family. Naming them is the deliverable — an implementer currently has to guess which to reach for.
components.rule: Anything truncated must carry a title. Any number must be able to name its field.

components.name: DataRow
components.claim: One record in a dense table.

variants.treatment: --panel2, eyebrow type, hairline below
hairline below, hover --panel2, radius 0
surface lift + count, makes the tier the visual unit
derivation panel inside the row container
dashed border + field name + what would fill it

components.rule: Radius 0. Hairlines, never zebra. Grid track sets must fit their pane at 924px.

components.name: Stepper
components.claim: Adjust a bounded numeric setting in place.

variants.treatment: − / + at 24×23px, flex:none
− / + / ↺ where the value can be pending

states: inert (job in flight — does not respond, reason in the banner)
components.rule: Inert, not hidden. Hiding a control mid-job makes the UI feel broken.

components.name: TypeAhead
components.claim: Commit a record from a ranked candidate list at keyboard speed.
requirements: autofocus on mount and re-assert on node attach
components.find: RESOLVED 26 Jul 2026 — Draft now specifies the Mock Lab implementation. One component, one key map.
components.rule: If a screen claims 'never needs the mouse', focus must be asserted on load.
components.randomise: candidate order is randomised so position does not encode confidence; probabilities travel with their rows
components.instrumentation: entry_mode logged per pick (shortcut | typed | pasted) so shortcut bias can be measured rather than argued

components.name: IdentityChip
components.claim: Who a player is, fast, with visual anchoring.

variants.note: the null state, and currently the only populated one

components.rule: Team colour is used here and for nothing else that carries data.

components.name: HeroBand
components.claim: What this screen is, plus the measured facts that frame it.
components.rule: Radius --r-m, --sh elevation, eyebrow + title + a strip of real numbers.

notCountedWhy: Each appears on exactly one surface and has no variants yet. Promote to a component the second a second screen needs it — that is the drift this inventory exists to catch.

files.note: Eight reference files cover twelve components. Stepper, TypeAhead and HeroBand share data-row.dc.html; IdentityChip shares chip.dc.html — each is anchored, not duplicated.
